title: digitalis purpurea proles dubia
intro: Digitalis purpurea proles dubia, commonly known as the lesser foxglove, is a plant species in the family Plantaginaceae, closely related to the common foxglove (Digitalis purpurea). The lesser foxglove is known for its potential health benefits, including the treatment of heart conditions such as atrial fibrillation and congestive heart failure, where it helps to slow the heart rate and increase its efficiency. The therapeutic actions of Digitalis purpurea proles dubia are attributed to its cardiac glycosides, specifically digitoxigenin and gitoxigenin, which act as positive inotropic agents, thereby increasing the contraction force of the heart muscle. The bioactive constituents of this plant include cardenolides and cardenolide glycosides, which contribute to its medicinal properties and are responsible for its therapeutic effects.
